query: The Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy forms several primary non-eutectic phases during solidification and exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence. Under rapid cooling, slower cooling, and subsequent reheating assessed by thermal analysis, what single intervention could increase amorphous retention and thermal stability while overcoming extensive primary crystallization? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to the alloy’s reported glass formation and crystallization behavior, the relevant cooling-rate and reheating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: A minor addition of 1 at.% boron to the Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy will suppress the multistep primary crystallization during moderate quenching and increase the thermal stability of the retained amorphous phase.  Boron increases liquid‐state viscosity and disrupts the chemical ordering that seeds primary intermetallics, thereby lowering their nucleation rate and raising the onset of crystallization in DSC.
generation.intervention: addition of 1 at.% B prior to melt spinning
generation.conditions: melt spinning at linear wheel speeds corresponding to cooling rates of 1×10^4 K/s (“rapid”) and 1×10^3 K/s (“slower”); subsequent DSC reheating at 20 K/min from room temperature to 800 K
generation.structural_mediator: enhanced liquid‐phase viscosity and local chemical heterogeneity around B atoms
generation.mechanism: B atoms preferentially occupy interstitial sites in the undercooled liquid, increasing atomic packing efficiency and viscosity; this suppresses nucleation of primary non‐eutectic phases and delays the first crystallization step
generation.predicted_outcome: At 1×10^4 K/s, amorphous fraction increases from ~60% (baseline) to >85%; at 1×10^3 K/s, it increases from ~10% to ≥50%.  DSC onset crystallization temperature (T_x) shifts upward by ≥15 K relative to undoped alloy.
generation.baseline: undoped Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20: ~60% amorphous at 1×10^4 K/s, ~10% at 1×10^3 K/s; T_x≈700 K at 20 K/min
generation.boundary: cooling rates between 1×10^3 and 1×10^4 K/s; reheating rate fixed at 20 K/min up to 800 K
generation.uncertainty: ±10% on amorphous fraction; ±5 K on T_x shift

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two series of melt‐spun ribbons (undoped vs 1 at.% B) at 1×10^4 and 1×10^3 K/s.  Quantify amorphous content by X‐ray diffraction (Rietveld refinement) and measure T_g and T_x by DSC at 20 K/min.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if the B‐doped alloy does not show at least a 30 ppt increase in amorphous fraction at 1×10^3 K/s and/or fails to exhibit a ≥10 K increase in T_x compared to the undoped alloy.
